purpose: Declared-failure ledger for `python scripts/check_forecast_invariants.py --sidecar-dir` (CI job `forecast-invariant-artifacts`, added by FFR-1D for audit finding FR-24). Every FAIL recorded in a committed run sidecar under frontend/data/hindcast/ must appear here, so a NEWLY registered run that fails an invariant is a reviewed line in this file rather than a number that lands on the forecast dashboard unremarked. Adding a line is not absolution: an invariant FAIL is a root-cause finding (rules 1/11), and the open ones are tracked in docs/forecast-readiness-audit-2026-07.md.
how_to_update: Registering a run whose sidecar carries a FAIL: add `"<run_id>": ["I4", ...]` below in the same commit as the registration, and name the finding it belongs to in your findings doc. Removing a run's sidecar, or fixing the defect so the invariant passes, means DELETING its line here — the checker fails on a stale declaration too.
seeded: 2026-07-31 (FFR-1D) from the invariant blocks committed at that date; re-seeded 2026-08-01 on the rebase onto the merged Wave-1 lanes (FFR-1A/1B/1C registrations). No verdict was changed at either point.
wave1_note: The FFR-1A arms are visible here as the fix they are: pjm-2026-2030-ffr1a-before and neiso-2026-2030-ffr1a-before carry I4, and neither of their arm1/arm2 successors does — the confirmed-exit derate ledgering (FR-1) closed I4 on both ISOs. The FFR-1C i7-before/after pairs still carry I7 on CAISO/MISO/NYISO: hydro accreditation narrowed the gap without closing it (that run's own findings doc records the residual). ercot-2026-2028-ffr1a-t0-* carry I3, the standing ERCOT energy-only scarcity-slack finding (FR-6), not anything those arms introduced.
ffr2b_note: FFR-2B (2026-08-02) declared five previously-undeclared runs, in the commit that repairs this job. FOUR ARE FFR-2B'S OWN and were the session's own miss — the runs were registered without their line here: miso-2021-2025-cmc-{legacy,pipeline}-ffr2b carry I9 (storage simultaneity, 0.36/0.56 % of throughput, BIT-IDENTICAL across the two arms and therefore not attributable to retirement_rule); miso-2026-2030-ffr2b-t1f-base carries I7 and -dampers carries I7 + I12. The T1-F pair's I7/I12 are the SUBSTANTIVE D-2 finding, not noise: arming entry_rate_limits + entry_commissioning_lag widens I7 from one failing year (2026) to three (2026-2028) and pushes I12 from WARN to FAIL, because the damped arm stops concealing an adequacy shortfall the base arm closed with an unbuildable 4.9 GW single-year gas_ct wave (MISO's actual 2021-25 gas_ct additions totalled 1.379 GW). Recorded as a disclosed cost of owner decision D-2, not tuned away (rule 1) — docs/handoffs/ffr-2b-retirement-entry-evidence-2026-08-02.md §1.3/§3. THE FIFTH IS NOT FFR-2B'S: ercot-2023-2025-t1ff-armr-fh1gate (I6, I7) is FH-1's §3.3 harness-defect gate probe, registered earlier the same day without a declaration, which left this CI job RED ON MAIN before FFR-2B merged. Declared here because it is accurate and unbreaks main; the verdict is unchanged and remains FH-1's — the I6 over-retirement REPRODUCES at the T1-FF posture (26.8 % of prior thermal in 2025) and FH-4/Phase A stays BLOCKED until a retirement-lane fix lands and FH-1's gate is re-probed (docs/handoffs/fh-1-full-forward-harness-2026-08.md §7).
